ri_table.source: Confirmed from the published source code (github.com/bpmsg/ahp-os, classes/AhpCalc.php): setAlonsoCr() computes CR = (lambda_max - n) / ((2.7699*n - 4.3513) - n), citing Alonso & Lamata (2006), and the priority calculator page (ahp-calc.php) displays exactly this value. At n = 4 the formula's effective RI is 0.909433, where Alonso & Lamata's Table 1 gives 0.8815 and the Saaty (1980) table 0.90. The documented formula is also stated in K. D. Goepel's AHP-OS implementation paper (IJAHP 10(3), 2018, working-paper eq. 2.5).

matrices.matrix.cr.note: Displayed '3.4%' (the tool's value is 0.0342) vs the fixture's expected 0.035281 under the Alonso-Lamata Table 1 values - outside tolerance. See the capture-level explanation.

explanation: The displayed CR (3.4%, i.e. 0.0342 by the tool's documented formula) differs from this fixture's expected 0.035281 even though both trace to Alonso & Lamata (2006): the fixture declares their Table 1 random-index values (RI(4) = 0.8815), while the tool implements their LINEAR FIT, CR = (lambda_max - n)/((2.7699n - 4.3513) - n), whose effective RI(4) is 0.9094. The same paper thus yields two CR conventions that differ by about four percent relative at this matrix size. Priorities and lambda_max match; the difference is entirely in the random-index convention.

reverify.instructions: Open https://bpmsg.com/ahp/ahp-calc.php (no account needed). Enter 4 criteria named P, Q, R, S; judgments: P 3 over Q, P 5 over R, P 8 over S, Q 3 over R, Q 5 over S, R 3 over S. Calculate and read the priorities, 'Consistency Ratio CR' and 'Principal eigen value'.
